table.brief: Bill of materials: Part number (like RC0402FR-0710KL) / Description (long) / Qty / Unit price / Supplier

understanding.purpose: Identify and source the parts needed to build a prototype controller board, with quantities and unit prices.
understanding.reading: Readers locate a part by number or description, then scan across its row to check quantity, price and supplier. The descriptions are much longer than the other values, so their wrapping will largely determine row height.
groups: Part number and description identify the component and its specifications.
Quantity and unit price support purchasing and cost comparisons.
Supplier complements the part number as a sourcing reference.
keep_intact: Part numbers and supplier names, especially long unbreakable identifiers.
Quantities and unit-price values, so they remain easy to compare.
may_wrap: Descriptions can wrap at spaces; shorter cells in the same row can occupy the resulting height.
The Unit price header can wrap if the price values remain readable.

preferred.name: r0A
preferred.note: Protect every column's longest unbreakable value and the one-line price width, giving the remaining space to naturally wrapping descriptions.

preferred.name: r2A
preferred.note: Give Unit price 11px more so its header fits on one line, taking that space from Description. Keep the identifier, quantity and supplier widths intact; check whether the narrower description introduces undesirable wrapping.

acceptable.name: r1A
acceptable.note: Move 11px from unit price to description. This preserves the widths needed for complete part numbers, supplier names, quantities and price values, while giving descriptions more room. The unit-price header will wrap, so the render should be checked for whether the improved description breaks justify the taller header.

acceptable.name: r3A
acceptable.note: Move 11px from unit price to description. This gives descriptions more room while retaining the stated 59px needed for the longest price value; the Unit price header may wrap.

bad.name: r0B
bad.note: Give descriptions more room while preserving part numbers, accepting a wrapped price header and possible breaks or overflow in long supplier names.
bad.why: The supplier column breaks STMicroelectronics across lines, making a repeated supplier harder to scan, while the Unit price header also wraps.

bad.name: r0C
bad.note: Prioritize readable descriptions and compact purchasing columns, accepting that the longest part numbers and supplier names may need to break or overflow.
bad.why: Part numbers and STMicroelectronics split mid-word. Breaking identifiers makes them harder to check and copy visually, despite the even row heights.

rationale: r0A and r2A are identical and give part numbers, prices, and suppliers enough room to stay intact, while all headers remain on one line. The description column takes the remaining width and wraps naturally, keeping each BOM item readable as a row. The microcontroller description takes three lines, but that is a reasonable cost for preserving the identifiers and supplier names.

general: Protect identifiers and other strings readers must verify from arbitrary mid-word breaks.
Allocate width according to content and reading task; a regular row height alone does not guarantee a readable table.
specific: The long part numbers and STMicroelectronics set useful minimum widths for the first and last columns.
Giving Unit price 91px keeps its header on one line without forcing a mid-word split elsewhere.

tradeoffs: r1A and r3A give descriptions slightly more space, but wrap the Unit price header and make the header row taller. A designer might prefer that allocation if description line breaks matter more than a compact, single-line header.
uncertain: The ranges are conservative estimates around the preferred widths, not browser-tested thresholds. They describe small coordinated adjustments within the 719px total; their endpoints are not intended to be combined independently.

critique.good: The compact header, intact part numbers and supplier names, and clear quantity and price columns support scanning across each row. Most descriptions occupy two lines.
critique.problems: The microcontroller description takes three lines and makes its row taller; its Cortex-M3 designation also breaks across lines. Some other descriptions wrap at awkward points.
critique.cause: The 241px description column leaves 220px for text. The 91px unit-price column keeps its header on one line but uses space that could help the descriptions.

critique.good: The wider description column improves several line breaks while preserving complete part numbers and readable price values.
critique.problems: STMicroelectronics splits within the name in two rows, making a sourcing reference harder to read. Other supplier names wrap, the price header takes two lines, and the microcontroller description still takes three lines.
critique.cause: The 131px supplier column leaves only 110px for text, less than the 133px needed by the longest unbreakable supplier name. The 80px price column leaves too little room for its header on one line.

critique.good: The wide description column keeps every description to two lines, giving the body rows a consistent rhythm. Quantities and prices remain easy to compare.
critique.problems: Two long part numbers and both instances of STMicroelectronics split within identifiers. The two-line price header also makes the header as tall as a body row.
critique.cause: The 160px part-number column leaves 139px for text, below the 165px needed by the longest identifier; the 126px supplier column leaves 105px, below the 133px needed. The 80px price column wraps its header.

critique.good: Part numbers, quantities, prices and supplier names remain intact, making each row easy to scan across. The description receives most of the flexible width, and its wrapping creates a consistent rhythm across most rows.
critique.problems: The Unit price header wraps onto two lines, making the header row taller and giving that short purchasing column more visual weight than it needs. The microcontroller description takes three lines, while the ESD description breaks the hyphenated term “2-line” across lines.
critique.cause: The 80px price column provides 59px for text, less than the header’s 70px one-line width. The 252px description column provides 231px for text, so longer descriptions wrap at available break points.

critique.good: The part numbers, quantities, prices and supplier names stay intact, and the headers are easy to scan. The identification columns lead naturally into purchasing and sourcing details. Most rows have a consistent two-line rhythm.
critique.problems: The description column feels cramped: the microcontroller description takes three lines, and hyphenated terms such as Cortex-M3 and 2-line break across lines. The longer part numbers and supplier names also sit close to their column edges.
critique.cause: At 241px, the description column has 220px for text. The 186px part-number and 154px supplier columns are already at their stated minimums for keeping their longest values intact. The 91px unit-price column has some space to spare.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r0A.why: Part numbers, prices, suppliers and headers stay intact, and rows scan clearly. The description column wraps Cortex-M3 and 2-line at hyphens, making those specifications slightly harder to read.

r1A.why: Identifiers and supplier names stay intact, while the description has enough room for mostly natural wrapping. The Unit price header wraps and 2-line breaks across lines.

r3A.why: Identifiers and supplier names stay intact, and descriptions scan reasonably well. The Unit price header wraps and 2-line breaks across lines.

r0B.why: The wider description column improves several line breaks, but supplier names wrap repeatedly and STMicroelectronics splits within the word. Unit price also wraps.

ref_auto.why: Part numbers and supplier names stay intact, with a balanced distribution of space and readable descriptions. The Unit price header wraps and 2-line breaks across lines.

ref_equal.why: Equal-width columns leave excessive space for quantities and prices while squeezing descriptions and part numbers. Identifiers and supplier names split, and tall rows make comparison difficult.

raw.unsure: B, C and E appear nearly identical at this scale. A keeps the Unit price header on one line, though its narrower description column creates an additional break in Cortex-M3.

r3A.why: Part numbers, prices and suppliers stay intact, and descriptions have a workable two- to three-line rhythm. The Unit price header wraps, making the header taller.

ref_auto.why: The proportions keep identifiers and suppliers intact while giving descriptions useful space. The Unit price header wraps, and the description column is slightly narrower than in A.

r0A.why: All headers fit on one line and identifiers and suppliers stay intact. The narrower description column creates less helpful breaks, including Cortex-M3 across lines.

r0B.why: The wider description column helps its text, but supplier names wrap frequently and STMicroelectronics breaks inside the word. The Unit price header also wraps.

ref_equal.why: Equal column widths give excessive space to quantity and price while squeezing descriptions into many short lines. Part numbers and supplier names break across lines, making rows harder to scan.

r1A.why: Identifiers, prices and suppliers stay intact, and the description column supports a consistent reading rhythm. The Unit price header wraps onto two lines.

raw.unsure: A and F appear visually identical at the shown resolution. C has a cleaner single-line header, but its narrower descriptions produce less natural breaks.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
